title: CoBia: Constructed Conversations Can Trigger Otherwise Concealed Societal Biases in LLMs
findings: Religion, along with race and orientation, generally showed lower bias scores compared to other categories like national origin. For example, the gemma2:27b model's bias score for religion remained below 0.2. The paper suggests this may indicate that these dimensions are more closely monitored through model safeguards or data filtering.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures societal biases against various socio-demographic groups, including religious groups. It evaluates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can recover from fabricated biased claims and reject biased follow-up questions in a constructed conversational setting.
